claims.statement: The fragment directs selection of Agent from the Chat dropdown. This is an interface action, not evidence of a launched task, approved tool execution, model entitlement, or active delegated agent.

The fragment reports GitHub's observation that many successful rollouts permit self-service license claiming without approval and links to setup options. It supplies no study denominator, causal proof, adopted license procedure, budget authorization, or applicable waiver of this project's approvals.

The semantic-index fragment says repository-context natural-language answering is optimized when the repository semantic search index is up to date. It specifies no freshness interval, index-completeness check, measured improvement, or evidence that this repository is indexed; the linked explanation is not reviewed here.

The next-steps list recommends adoption-oriented governance through delegation, prompt enablement of vetted features and aligned spend controls; exploring self-service licenses; planned enablement; training with Spaces and code review; and cloud-agent asynchronous issue work. These linked recommendations do not establish feature vetting, approved expenditure, safe context sharing, delegated authority, actual training, or an authorized native pilot. None is adopted or performed from source advice.

The sign-in fragment conditionally requires settings changes before sign-in for a managed user on the data-residency site. It does not identify the settings in isolation or prove the user's identity/tenant applicability; no sign-in, credential, or residency setting was changed.

The Microsoft Enterprise Agreement fragment describes connecting an Azure subscription ID to the enterprise account as a prerequisite to enabling and paying for Copilot and links to billing instructions. This is not authority to access billing, expose an identifier, link accounts, incur costs, or treat the user's enterprise as covered by that agreement.
